createworkers.ponder.hard_hat.text_3: The first Right-Click marks a block as an Input, a second turns it into an Output

createworkers.ponder.hard_hat.text_5: A programmed Hat is a job. The next page hands one to somebody
createworkers.ponder.worker_station.head: Putting Workers to Work
createworkers.ponder.worker_station.text: A Worker Station is where a factory's jobs live, and where Villagers are taken on
Right-Click it to open the rack, and put a programmed Hard Hat into a slot
A Villager nearby that it can walk to is taken on for the job
It wears a copy of the Hat. The Hat itself stays in the rack
Then it works the Hat's beat, carrying items from the Inputs to the Outputs
Because the job never leaves the block, a Worker that is lost leaves it behind — and the next Villager along takes it up
A rack holds up to twelve jobs, and each one can run on any of the three shifts
Its face is the roster: one lamp per job, lit when the job has all its Workers and dim when it is short
Take a Hat back out to end its job and let its Workers go
createworkers.ponder.working_hours.text_: A Worker's day has four parts: its shift, an evening of its own, sleep, and a muster before the next shift starts
A job can run up to three crews — day, evening and night — so one Hat can be covered around the clock
Whatever is already in their hands is delivered first — nobody clocks off holding a stack
Off the clock they are villagers again — they wander, gossip and trade until it is time to turn in
Sneak and Right-Click a Bed while holding the Hat to say where that Worker sleeps
Given no Bed, they find an unclaimed one near their work — but only one they can walk to
Right-Click an Enderman with a Hat to put it to work. They keep no hours, so a line staffed with them runs through the night
A crew is woken before its shift and walks to its post, so the work is covered the moment the last crew stops
